title: Hoeveel kost het?
subtitle: Numbers 20-100 and prices
intro: After this lesson you can count from 20 to 100, ask and understand prices, and pay in a small shop. You will also learn how to say amounts in euros and cents.

example.en: One hundred cents is one euro.
My brother is twenty-one years old.
My sister is twenty-two years old.

words.note: Use kost for one item and kosten for two or more.

grammar.title: Numbers from 20 to 100
grammar.explanation: For 21-99, Dutch says the unit first, then **en**, then the ten: **eenentwintig** is one-and-twenty. The tens are **twintig, dertig, veertig, vijftig, zestig, zeventig, tachtig, negentig, honderd**.

grammar.title: Prices: 2,50 and kost/kosten
grammar.explanation: Dutch prices use a comma: **2,50** is two euros fifty. Say **twee euro vijftig**, not **twee komma vijftig**. Ask **Hoeveel kost het?** or **Wat kost de koffie?** Use **kost** for one thing; use **kosten** for two or more things.

examples.nl: De koffie kost twee euro vijftig.
examples.en: The coffee costs two euros fifty.

examples.nl: De koffie en de melk kosten samen drie euro vijftig.
examples.en: The coffee and the milk cost three euros fifty together.

grammar.tip: If there are two or more things, use **kosten**.

grammar.title: Paying: contant or pinnen
grammar.explanation: **Contant** means cash; **pinnen** means paying by card. Ask **Kan ik pinnen?** and say **Ik betaal contant.** Ask for a receipt with **Een bonnetje?**
grammar.tip: In many Dutch shops you can pay by card; a few are card-only (no cash).

mistakes.pattern: Uses plural 'kosten' with singular 'de koffie' (Hoeveel kosten de koffie?)
mistakes.explain: De koffie is one thing, so use 'kost': 'Hoeveel kost de koffie?'

mistakes.pattern: Puts the verb at the end (Hoeveel de koffie kost?)

mistakes.pattern: Uses both 'is' and 'kost' (Hoeveel is kost de koffie?)
mistakes.explain: Use either 'is' or 'kost', not both: 'Hoeveel is de koffie?' or 'Hoeveel kost de koffie?'

mistakes.pattern: Uses the opposite 'duur' (Dat is duur.)

culture.title: Prijzen en betalen in Nederland
culture.text: In Dutch shops prices are written with a comma: 2,50 means two euros fifty, not two hundred fifty. A growing number of shops and cafés are card-only, so you may see alleen pinnen; smaller shops and markets often still take cash. Keep your bonnetje if you need to return something.

summary: Count from 20 to 100 by learning the tens and the one-and-twenty pattern.
Say prices with euro and cent: 2,50 = twee euro vijftig.
Use kost for one item and kosten for two or more.
Ask Kan ik pinnen? and say Ik betaal contant.
